Brand mentions were scored by upvotes, placement (title, body, comment), and comment depth.

Those scores were then ranked against brand recommendations from ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini across 50 product queries, each asked three times. The correlation analysis spans 12 consumer categories.

A second test compared Reddit citations in 60 API calls (15 queries) vs. 100 web UI queries per platform, collected via browser automation in February 2026.

Key findings:

• Reddit brand rankings and AI brand rankings lined up fairly strongly.
• Web UIs cited Reddit in 44% of queries on Google AI Mode, 20% on Perplexity, and 17% on ChatGPT.
• APIs returned 0% Reddit citations on every platform.
• Opinion and comparison queries pulled in Reddit most often: 70.8% on Google AI Mode and 45.8% on Perplexity.
• Claude cited Reddit zero times in both channels, but it cited any source in only 19% of web UI queries.

Now, how I read it.

Reddit may influence LLM recommendations even when it’s not cited.

Shilling is also not the answer.

Engagement quality > raw mention volume.

Because the Reddit score included upvotes, title/body placement, and comment depth, the implied signal is a brand showing up in substantive, highly engaged discussions.

Reddit = reputation channel.

I definitely need to research more guerrilla tactics on Reddit. For now, I’m just passively growing karma—but I’m not sure how to inject brand discussions without it becoming shilling / spam.

SÅ ER CENSURDEMOKRATERNE PÅ SPIL IGEN

Som en, der har prøvet at få en gedigen tur i den politiske vridemaskine under Covid, ved jeg, hvilket pres Peter Ernstved er under i de her dage, efter han skrev en kronik om forhandlingerne i Ukraine.

Man kan mene, hvad man vil om Ernstveds leder (jeg er uenig i den), men sidst jeg orienterede mig, var vi et frit land, hvor man ikke blev udsat for offentligt pres fra ministre, hvis man anlagde et synspunkt, som ikke flugter med den officielle danske holdning.

Det var nøjagtigt det samme, jeg blev udsat for under Covid. Da jeg afslørede, at registerkørsler ledte til dobbelt-counting af indlæggelser med Covid, og da jeg med de første studier fra blandt andet Gibraltar kunne afdække, at vaccinen IKKE forhindrede smittespredning, så trådte Socialdemokraterne til (både herhjemme og i flere af vores nabolande) og krævede min afgang hos Nordea.

Jeg er mildest talt rystet over, at det efterhånden er ved at være en præcedens, at man skal presses ud helt oppe fra allerøverste hold af ministre, hvis man siger noget, som ikke passer ind i partilinjen.

Og de her offentlige pressioner kommer vel at mærke fra et parti, som (u)bevidst har slettet evidens fra Covid-tiden, har nægtet at forholde sig til, om man lavede fejl, og så videre. En ekstrem magtfuldkommenhed, som nu igen går ud over Peter Ernstved.

Det er faktisk decideret udansk, hvis jeg skal sige det lige ud, i de her tider, hvor danskhed debatteres. Hvor ville jeg dog have LANGT mere respekt for politikere, som værnede om det frie ord, som kunne erkende fejl, og som kunne udvise transparens, når tingene ikke er gået efter planen. Intet af det kan man sige om Socialkammeraterne, som er på slisken til at opføre sig mere og mere og mere autoritært. Alt sammen på Mette Frederiksens vagt.

Vi trænger til en ny statsminister. Ganske enkelt.

LayerZero unlocks another 23.6M ZRO for core contributors and partners, about 5.9% of what's circulating.

Last time ZRO dropped about 15% the week after. If it starts sliding before the 19th I'd take that as a warning.

Ethena has two unlocks back to back, about 266M ENA going to ecosystem incentives, the foundation, contributors and investors.

ENA's been unlocking on a schedule like this for a while now. I'd watch how it handles the 2nd before guessing at the 5th.

36.8M EIGEN goes to investors and early contributors, roughly 3.8% of circulating supply. Last unlock it barely moved, down under 3% over the week.

There are two kinds of stocks where you should assume you have little or no alpha: companies with a market cap above $100 billion, followed by analysts everywhere, and stocks followed by everyone on X—especially ones being pushed by stock influencers with four-year track records.

Screaming that a company trades at a P/E of 16 isn’t an edge. Everyone has the numbers on their desk. Plenty of smart analysts are following these companies. You might still invest in them, but understand that you probably don’t have alpha just because you spotted a familiar metric.

I look for opportunities in $1–5 billion companies I know well. When a smaller company falls, there may be nobody waiting to buy. Only a few people follow it, and the big holders already own a lot. That can make selling unusually aggressive. $WGS fell 17% in one day, with no news and about three times normal volume. If I wanted out of a position like that, I’d spread the selling over a week. Why dump it all in one day at triple the volume? It looked like someone needed out fast.

Make a habit of knowing 12 companies very well. When one falls 15%, check for news or an earnings announcement, then use what you know about the business to judge whether something has really changed—or whether someone may be stuck and selling fast. That’s when you may find a dislocation worth acting on.

There are two kinds of stocks where you should assume you have little or no alpha: companies with a market cap above $100 billion, followed by analysts everywhere, and stocks followed by everyone on X—especially ones being pushed by stock influencers with four-year track records.

Screaming that a company trades at a P/E of 16 isn’t an edge. Everyone has the numbers on their desk. Plenty of smart analysts are following these companies. You might still invest in them, but understand that you probably don’t have alpha just because you spotted a familiar metric.

I look for opportunities in $1–5 billion companies I know well. When a smaller company falls, there may be nobody waiting to buy. Only a few people follow it, and the big holders already own a lot. That can make selling unusually aggressive. $WGS fell 17% in one day, with no news and about three times normal volume. If I wanted out of a position like that, I’d spread the selling over a week. Why dump it all in one day at triple the volume? It looked like someone needed out fast.

Make a habit of knowing 12 companies very well. When one falls 15%, check for news or an earnings announcement, then use what you know about the business to judge whether something has really changed—or whether someone may be stuck and selling fast. One important aspect of stock trading is not to get too complacent about the fact that they have smaller drawdowns than altcoins and feel 'safer'

Meaning, you can theoretically "average down" into a dip, but you have to:
1/ be very surgical about where you add (only on new local lows)
2/ de-risk on bounces
3/ know how many chips you have left so that you still have some if we reach an extreme drawdown (which would be 'deep value' to buy in the context of the LTF move)

It's also extremely easy to be buying a local top while feeling comfortable, without realizing you are actually at a very risky level for bulls

As usual, the main risk management lesson is all about one word: sizing.
Oversizing a trade is the main thing you should always try to avoid

ALERT🚨: The number of tokens that can be cached can increase by 20-40%🚀 by enabling DRAM KVCache offloading optimization at 12-16 concurrent agentic sessions. A B200 only has 180 GB of HBM, and after weight storage, only 100 GB of HBM per chip remains for KVCache.

THIS IS NOT ENOUGH FOR LONG-CONTEXT AGENTIC INFERENCE WORKLOADS. Thus, with SGLang HiCache, you can also offload KVCache to the CPU's DDR5/LPDDR5X memory, which helps improve performance. (1/2)🧵
